ModMetadata.Name: Cable Labels
ModMetadata.Author: erica-kretsch
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]Cable Labels[/h1]
Pipes have labels; cables don't. Behind a wall panel or in a busy conduit, three red cables look the same until you trace them. This mod adds a cable label: the vanilla pipe label, made thinner to fit a cable, so you can name each run where you can see it.
Idea by Kastuk.
[h2]How to use it[/h2] [list] [*]Print a [b]Kit (Cable Label)[/b] at the Electronics Printer, for 1 iron. [*]Place it on a straight stretch of cable, as you would a cable fuse. It won't go on a corner, a junction or a broken cable. [*]Name it with the Labeller. The name shows on both sides of the label. [/list]
[h2]Details[/h2] [list] [*]The label fits itself to the cable it's on: normal, heavy and super-heavy. [*]Like the pipe label, it has open gaps at the top and bottom. If you're looking into one, roll the label as you place it (Insert / Page Up) so its text faces you. [*]One label per cell. A cable fuse or cable analyser can still be placed where a label is, so a label never gets in the way of an urgent fix. [*]It comes apart with the same tool as a pipe label. [/list]
[h2]Multiplayer[/h2] Install it on the server and on every player: it adds a new structure, which a player without the mod doesn't have. Removing the mod from a save removes the cable labels placed in it, and nothing else.
[h2]Support[/h2] Report a bug or ask for a change on GitHub: https://github.com/erica-kretsch/cable-labels/issues
[h2]For modders[/h2] A label measures the cable it's on, so it fits any round modded cable with no work from you. For a cable that isn't round, or whose meshes reach beyond the cable itself, a small interface you copy into your own mod tells labels how to fit, without referencing this one. The GitHub README explains how.
This is a [b]StationeersLaunchPad[/b] mod. It requires BepInEx. See: https://github.com/StationeersLaunchPad/StationeersLaunchPad
